lines.note: Mǒxicauaxi means exchanging speech or entering into conversation. The caron is visible; its continuation gives the interlocutors.
Falar com outros completes the definition as speaking with others. This is a short continuation of the conversational verb.
Mǒxicaye means retracting or changing what one has said. The faint caron is visible, and Desdizerſe corrects OCR Dendizerſe.
The second gloss is amending what has been said. The scan supports final à in està, not OCR i, while the physical em-mendar division is preserved.
Mǒxicayouaxi means making messages go back and forth. The causative communication sense continues over the next two rows.

runs.text: com recados, ou communicarſe com algum por

lines.note: The gloss concerns exchanging messages or communicating with someone. Communicarſe retains its doubled m and long ſ.
Communication is by letter or message. This closes the definition without adding a modern distinction between written and oral media.
Mǒxicoxi means sending word or sending someone to say something. The printed oita principal form is retained.

Moxicuua is equated with Xijen and glossed as 'perhaps' or the conjunction 'or'. The o remains unmarked. The final written-register label S. is upright in the scan, outside the italic Portuguese gloss.
Mǒxicuuaye means adding someone to the number of others through speech or intercession. The word numero is divided after nu-.

runs.text: mero de outros falando, ou intercedendo, &c.

lines.note: This completes the explanation of adding by speaking or interceding. The scan has falando without the OCR's extra u.

runs.text: Mǒxidaxi, ſu, aita. l, Mǒxi idaxi, ſu.

lines.note: Mǒxidaxi and Mǒxi idaxi are explicitly alternative forms. The Portuguese Co- is italic with its line-end hyphen and is completed below.

runs.text: meçar a dizer, ou mouer pratica.

lines.note: The gloss is beginning to speak or opening a conversation. It completes Co-meçar while preserving the physical line break.
Mǒxifanaxi means dismissing something by words or speaking decisively. The divided pa-lauras is retained across the next row.
The second gloss specifies speaking resolutely. This completes the same entry, not a separate synonym headword.
Mǒxifayaxi means praising or extolling something in conversation. The second Portuguese infinitive is divided after encare-.
Cer completes encarecer, extolling something in conversation. The abbreviation tilde in algũa is retained.

Mǒxifiraqi means explaining or giving reasons in defence. The scan appears to print final a in rezãa, unlike rezão two rows below; that anomaly is retained. The space after ẽ and the divided de-fenſa preserve the physical setting.
The defence gloss ends and a Japanese example begins, stating the grounds or substance of one's reasoning. Dǒrino and mǒxi both visibly have carons.
Firaite completes the Japanese example of explaining the grounds. Xid. is a wholly roman citation label, not the OCR's mixed Xi/d styling; here rezão ends with o.
Rezoando completes arrezoando, giving reasons or making an argument. The word remains divided at the physical line break.
Mǒxifuraxi means spreading a report or making something public. The scan supports f in both furaxi and fama, correcting the OCR's r and long ſ respectively.
Blicar completes publicar, to make public. This is the end of the spreading-a-report definition.
Mǒxifure means announcing publicly or making known. The worn f has a surviving upper trace; the proclamation gloss supports fure rather than the OCR's rure.
A ſaber completes fazer a ſaber, making something known. The short continuation belongs to the announcement entry.
Mǒxifuzzucuri means seeking something through negotiation or verbal contrivance. A faint caron survives over the damaged first o; the doubled zz and printed uru, utta remain unchanged.

runs.text: palaura, ou com inuenção de palauras procu-

lines.note: The gloss specifies negotiation by speech or by devising words. The worn but recoverable u in palauras corrects OCR palaaras; procu- continues below.
Rar completes procurar, seeking to obtain something. This closes the verbal-negotiation definition.
Mǒxigoto is a saying or utterance. The noun is distinguished from the surrounding inflected verbs.
The separately printed Mǒxi daxi points back to Mǒxidaxi. The visible spacing and absence of an additional i before daxi are retained rather than normalized from the earlier alternative form.
Mǒxi ire means telling someone. The o has a caron, correcting the OCR's circumflex.
The example concerns conveying notice or information. The scan supplies the omitted paragraph mark and the x in mǒxi, replacing the malformed mǒ ci; the Portuguese keeps the printed joined aſaber.

runs.text: Carta, ou eſcrito em que ſe darazão

lines.note: Mǒxijo is a letter or document giving an account of something. The visible c in eſcrito corrects OCR eſerito; the printed joined darazão is retained. The headword's final o has no established accent, so the lexical index's Mǒxijǒ is not substituted for this copy's form.
Dalgũa couſa completes the matter explained in the document. Its abbreviation tilde remains unexpanded.
Mǒximauaxi means sending notice around or publishing it in different places. The mark over o is read as a caron, not the OCR's circumflex.

runs.text: blicar por diuerſas partes. ¶ Item, per met.

lines.note: This completes publicar por diuerſas partes and introduces a metaphorical extension. The scan indents the continuation, unlike the unindented OCR line marker.
The extended sense is speaking or saying various things. Per met. in the preceding row explicitly signals this figurative use.
Mǒxi midaxi means confusing or disturbing through words. Perturbar ends in r, not OCR s; embu continues below without an invented hyphen.
Rulhar completes emburulhar, here tangling or confusing through speech. The division and historical form are retained.
Mǒxi muſubi means negotiating or arranging something verbally with another person. The printed u, unda principal forms remain unchanged.
This completes negotiating verbally with someone and begins Yenpen, the marriage-arrangement example continued on the next row. The paragraph mark is part of the printed line.
Yenpen uo mǒximuſubu means arranging a marriage or betrothal by negotiation. The Portuguese ends at deſpo-, whose continuation belongs to the next physical row.
The continuation completes deſpoſorios, followed by marriage arranged verbally. The first vowel is o, correcting OCR ſarios; the historical spelling is not modernized.
Mǒxin, explained by Midarina cocoro, is a disordered or troubled heart. The damaged middle of Midarina is consistent with that reading; the Portuguese adjective continues below.

runs.text: nado, ou perturbado com ruins penſamintos.

lines.note: The heart is described as disturbed by bad thoughts. The scan reads perturbado without the OCR's extra syllable and internal gap; the anomalous penſamintos is retained rather than changed to pensamentos.
Mǒxinadame means soothing or appeasing through words. The abbreviation cõ is preserved, and the Portuguese paraphrase distinguishes this from merely reporting speech.

This is Moxinarauaxi, an expression being current in speech, illustrated at the top of column 2. The headword and aita are heavily abraded; the surviving sequence and the ensuing mǒxinarauaſu support the restored letters, also identified by NINJAL 168a23. No caron is supplied where none can be securely seen over this headword's o. Lexical identifications are aids, not substitutes for this scan's spelling or typography.
The example says that something circulates in common speech. The gloss begins Correr algũa, correcting OCR Carrer algãa; it continues the headword at the foot of column 1.
Couſa no pouo completes the description of a saying or report current among the people, not a new entry.
Mǒxinauoxi means correcting what was said. The article before dito is o, not OCR e; the principal forms and caron are legible.
Deſdizerſe supplies the alternative sense of retracting one's words. The short continuation belongs to Mǒxinauoxi.
Mǒxinaxi is explaining a matter in terms of how it occurs. The noun is couſa, not conſa; ma- is the printed first part of maneira.

runs.text: neira que ſe faz, ou paßa. ¶ Item, Fa-

lines.note: This completes maneira que ſe faz, ou paßa, then starts a further sense with Falar divided as Fa-. The printed double-s ligature in paßa is preserved.

runs.text: lar bem, ou mal ſobre algum negocio.

lines.note: The additional sense is speaking well or ill about some matter. Lar completes Falar across the physical line break.
Mǒxinobe is glossed as extending or enlarging upon something in words. Dilatar contains the l omitted by the OCR; the Portuguese explanation continues below.
Palauras completes the explanation of Mǒxinobe: the expansion or extension is verbal. This is a separate short physical continuation.
Mǒxinocoxi means leaving something unsaid. The line ends with al-, continued as gũa on the next row.
Gũa couſa completes algũa couſa, the thing omitted from one's speech. The nasal abbreviation is not expanded.
Mǒxinogare means extricating or defending oneself by giving an explanation. The Portuguese noun razão is split at ra-.
Zão deſi completes giving an account of oneself. The printed joined deſi is preserved rather than respaced as modern de si.
Mǒxiqicaxe means telling someone and making them hear. The printed principal form ſuru is retained, not regularized to uru.
The complement a outros identifies the people made to hear what is said. The historical u/v spelling in ouuir is retained.

Mǒxiqiri means speaking decisively. The scan gives itta with two t's and a comma after ru and after determinação, correcting the OCR's ita and periods; the printed ru is not replaced by the lexical index's u.
The continuation adds speaking resolutely to the preceding definition of Mǒxiqiri. The ampersand links it to determinação, rather than beginning an independent entry.
Mǒxiqiuame is speaking so as to reach a conclusion. The principal forms uru, eta and the caron over o are retained from the printed row.
Mǒxiſague means lowering or diminishing something through speech. The long s in the Japanese headword is distinguished from f by the word and the surviving type.
Com palauras specifies that the lowering or depreciation in the preceding entry is done verbally, not physically.
Mǒxiſaqe is breaking up a friendship by speech. The Portuguese initial is Q in Quebrar, not OCR O; the headword's diacritic is worn, so the aligned caron is retained rather than changed to an acute.

runs.text: algũs, ou fazer que não ſeão amigos.

lines.note: The definition is completed as making people cease to be friends. The abbreviated algũs and the historical ſeão are retained.
Mǒxiſaxi means stopping short in one's speech or not finishing it. The principal form is aita, correcting OCR aira; the scan's joined apratica is not modernized.
The alternative gloss is interrupting the discourse. Interrompela is printed continuously, without the spurious OCR gap or a supplied modern clitic hyphen.
Mǒxi ſonji means making an error in speaking. The visible separation before ſonji and the principal forms zuru, ita are kept.
Mǒxiſumaxi means saying something perfectly or properly. The gloss reads perfeitamen-, correcting peifeitamen-; no comma is supplied between the lemma and ſu where the scan has none.
Te completes perfeitamente, and ou bem gives the plainer equivalent of saying something well. The original physical division is preserved.
Mǒxiſume is explaining or clarifying something verbally. The printed period after the headword is retained rather than regularized to a principal-form comma.

runs.text: com palauras, ou concluir, & acabar algũa cou-

lines.note: The gloss also allows bringing a matter to a conclusion through words. Cou- continues as ſa on the next row, preserving the printed split.
Demanda supplies a lawsuit or dispute as an example of the matter concluded. This completes the preceding definition rather than belonging to the next lemma.

The gloss Perſuadir identifies the intended word as the persuasion verb catalogued by NINJAL as Mǒxi susume (168b15). This copy nevertheless visibly prints Mǒxiſume, so the missing syllable is not silently supplied; the duplicate-looking lemma is retained with this caveat.
Mǒxiſute is glossed as speaking while leaving something unsaid. The printed tçuru principal form is retained, and the object of deixar por dizer follows below.
Dizer algũa couſa completes leaving some matter unsaid. The line belongs to Mǒxiſute, not the following entry.
Mǒxitate is explaining or arguing a case at length. The Portuguese arrezoar is divided after arrezo-, and the printed tçuru form remains unchanged.

runs.text: ar bem, & difuſamente por pontos, ou por or

lines.note: This specifies arguing well, expansively, point by point or in order. The scan separates ar bem and ends with or, not OCR os; ordem continues on the next row without a supplied hyphen.
Dem completes ordem; the example Dǒriuo mǒxitatçuru illustrates setting out one's reasons. Its Portuguese translation starts Ar- at the right edge and continues below.

runs.text: rezoar, ou dar razão desta maneira.

lines.note: This completes Arrezoar and paraphrases the example as giving reasons in this manner. Enlargement locates the low body of s beneath the left-reaching head of t in desta; the aligned round s is retained, rather than changing the connected type to long ſ.
Mǒxitçucuxi is exhausting a subject in speech. The printed principal form uita is retained, and the gloss continues with a simpler equivalent below.
Ou dizer tudo supplies that equivalent: saying everything. The short row completes the preceding entry.

runs.text: O q̃ leua recados, ou intercede.

lines.note: Mǒxitçugui denotes someone who carries messages or intercedes. Intercede has nt, correcting OCR imercede; the q with abbreviation tilde remains unexpanded.
Mǒxitçume means convincing or refuting someone through words. The gloss ends in pa-, whose continuation is on the next row.
Lauras completes palauras: the conviction or refutation is verbal. This very short physical row remains separately represented.
Mǒxitçuqe first means ordering or commanding. The Portuguese ordenar is divided after orde-, with no omitted intermediate text.

runs.text: nar. ¶ Item, Cuſtumar a dizer. Vt,

lines.note: This completes ordenar and adds being accustomed to saying something. The example starts Cõ-, a nasalized loanword fragment continued below; its horizontal abbreviation mark is not the OCR's caron.

The example concerns being accustomed to confession, with Mǒxi nareta recommended as the better expression across the next line. The scan supports the nasal mark in fisãouo and the caron in Mǒxi; the worn s in fisãouo is conservatively retained as the aligned round s.

runs.text: Estou ja cuſtumado à me confeßar.

lines.note: Nareta completes the recommended alternative. The Portuguese says that the speaker is already accustomed to confessing. Estou and cuſtumado correct OCR Eslou and cuſtamado; the st type is retained with the aligned round s after enlargement, while ja and the printed double-s ligature remain unchanged.

Mǒxitçutaye means transmitting by oral tradition. The damaged initial is M, not OCR A; tra ends the body row without a visible hyphen. The separate lower-right catchword dição. anticipates the continuation of tradição rather than being merged into this row.
